h1:
Where to stay in
Old City (inside the moat)
intro: Inside the moat (the old walled town) is the heart of Chiang Mai and the obvious choice for a first visit. Major temples like Wat Phra Singh and Wat Chedi Luang, plus the Tha Phae Gate, are all a short walk apart. On Sunday evenings, Ratchadamnoen Road turns into a long walking street where you can eat and shop late into the night. This is a walk-first neighbourhood with narrow lanes and traffic during festivals, so strolling or renting a bicycle beats driving in. The picks below run from a family-run guesthouse to an upper-end Lanna boutique.

blocks.html: Short answer: Inside the moat is Chiang Mai's best base for walking, with Wat Phra Singh, Wat Chedi Luang, and the Sunday Walking Street all within strolling distance of each other. Stays range from a few-hundred-baht guesthouse to Lanna-style boutiques in the low thousands. The trade-offs are narrow lanes, limited parking, and big Sunday-night crowds.

blocks.text: Recommended hotels in Old City (inside the moat)

items.name: Tri Gong Residence
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Budget · quiet seekers · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A small, family-run guesthouse of about 17 rooms on a quiet lane in the northeast corner of the moat, near Sompet Market and within walking distance of Tha Phae Gate and the walking street. Rooms have air-con, a TV, and free water. Reviews praise the kind, helpful owners and the calm location, with a guest score around 8.6. There's no pool and the building is plain, so it suits budget travellers who don't need fancy facilities.

items.name: Wannamas Chiangmai Boutique House
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Next to Wat Phra Singh · easy walking · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A small boutique house on Samlarn Road Soi 1, just a few steps from Wat Phra Singh. The decor is warm Thai-style and rooms are clean and compact, with free bicycles to borrow. Reviews praise the homemade breakfast, including homemade jam, and a location that makes walking the Old City effortless. The catch is tricky parking and fairly narrow stairs, so it fits couples or travellers who want to be right by the temples.

items.name: De Lanna Hotel
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Mid-range value · has a pool · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A 4-star hotel done in contemporary Lanna style in the middle of the moat, near Tha Phae Gate and Ratchadamnoen Road. It has an outdoor pool, a poolside bar, a rooftop terrace, and an on-site restaurant. Reviews praise the clean, spacious rooms and a breakfast with plenty of choice. It's good value compared with similar hotels in Chiang Mai, making it a solid pick for couples or families who want a pool without paying a lot.

items.name: Cheeva Dee Hotel
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Couples · small boutique · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A small-scale boutique about 500 metres from Wat Phra Singh. The highlights are spacious rooms and large bathrooms, with some rooms offering a bathtub and balcony, plus an outdoor pool and bikes to borrow. Reviews praise the cleanliness, attentive service, and breakfast. It costs a touch more than the area average because of the small room count and the privacy that brings, so it suits couples after a calm base in the Old City.

items.name: 99 The Heritage Hotel
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Temple view · opposite Wat Phra Singh · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A handsome boutique directly opposite Wat Phra Singh, which makes flagging a songthaew or tuk-tuk easy and puts temple visits right at the door. It has a small outdoor pool, a green garden, and free bicycles, and many rooms have a private balcony. Reviews consistently praise the attentive staff, the cleanliness, and an a-la-carte breakfast. A great fit for couples who want to wake up to a temple view in the Old City.

items.name: Phra Singh Village
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Lanna architecture · saltwater pool · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: An in-town resort in authentic Lanna style about 200 metres from Wat Phra Singh, built with wooden pavilions and leafy gardens. It has a saltwater pool, a spa, a gym, and bikes to borrow. Reviews praise the large, clean rooms, the garden breakfast, and friendly staff. The pool is on the small side but the mood is peaceful. It suits travellers who want a full Lanna atmosphere in a central Old City spot.

items.name: Rachamankha
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Quiet luxury · Lanna art and antiques · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A luxury Relais & Chateaux hotel of about 24 rooms and suites, set right against the old city wall, a one-minute walk from Wat Phra Singh and two minutes from the walking street. It's built around wide Lanna-style courtyards filled with Asian art and antiques, with a pool, a spa, and a well-known restaurant. Couples rate it around 9.7. To keep things peaceful it only accepts children over 12, so it suits travellers who want genuinely quiet, refined surroundings.

faq.q: Do I need to rent a car in the Old City, or is it walkable?
faq.a: You don't need a car to get around. Wat Phra Singh, Wat Chedi Luang, Tha Phae Gate, and the Sunday Walking Street are all within walking distance of each other. Parking is scarce and the lanes are narrow, so walking or renting a bicycle is the better option. For farther trips like Doi Suthep or Nimman, a red songthaew, taxi, or Grab is easier than driving yourself.

faq.q: Is the Sunday Walking Street noisy at night, and which room should I pick?
faq.a: On Sunday evenings, Ratchadamnoen Road becomes a walking street from afternoon until late, and it gets busy and lively. If your hotel is on a main road you may hear some of it, though it's not as loud as a bar district. For a quieter sleep, ask for a room facing inward or pick a place set back on a smaller lane. If you enjoy the buzz, staying near the walking street is handy, since you can just step out to eat and shop.

faq.q: What's the difference between the Old City and outside the moat (Nimman), and which is better?
faq.a: The Old City suits first-timers who want to walk among temples and soak up the old-town feel, with local-style restaurants and cafes at friendly prices. Nimman, just west of the moat, leans toward stylish cafes, modern restaurants, and the Maya mall, which appeals to cafe-hoppers and remote workers. If your trip is mainly temples and the walking street, choose the Old City; if it's cafes and lifestyle, go for Nimman.
